blocks.title: What changed since the last Report

runs.text: - CP-2D: reconcile accessible cash, committed distributions, working-capital funding and facility conditions into a separately evidenced liquidity bridge; do not net later events into September balances here. - CP-2G: develop forward cash-retention and acquired-earnings cases only after organic, capex, interest and normalization inputs are checked; keep FY2025 valuation points outside cash forecasts. - CP-3C: examine refinancing dependencies, securitization renewal and conditional bridge takeout with dated executable funding evidence; historical access is not future feasibility. - CP-4: review executed agreements, guarantees/collateral and amendments for actual legal permissions; annual disclosures, announced commitments and completed financing are not capacity opinions. - CP-5: validate material claim-to-handoff lineage, exact hashes, dates, units, definition conflicts and inherited limits; distinguish upstream checks from independent evidence certification. - CP-6: challenge the operating-resilience/retention thesis against its strongest countercases, especially durable differentiated margins versus persistent extraction; committee debate remains downstream.

These are targeted responsibilities, not claims that downstream modules ran. Preserve this incremental CP-2 separately from B and preserve P/V/W as distinct dated deliverables with their tables, definitions, provenance and restrictions. Existing delivery should retain this reasoning in the report/HTML and verify populated artifacts separately. No workbook, new engine, analytical rebuild, publication execution or full-pathway completion is claimed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Assessment — Analyst Interpretation; confidence Medium.** The historical thesis survives and becomes sharper: TDG's operating/cash advantages are substantive, but unusually large debt claims on annual cash generation and demonstrated extraction keep cash retention—not margin superiority—the deciding creditor variable. P strengthens B's operating counterweight while strengthening its debt-burden concern. V adds a warning against translating operating quality directly into valuation support. W adds acquisition-pricing and execution context, not TDG valuation evidence. Basis: B Assessment/priority findings; P T4.3–T4.7; V valuation conclusion; W transaction evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Thesis — Analyst Interpretation.** Installed-product economics and observed cash generation support historical debt service, but creditor improvement requires retained accessible cash and disciplined capital allocation; neither a peer margin advantage nor conditional value indications establish that retention. Basis: B Thesis and ranked weaknesses; P cash-funding discussion; V/W restrictions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Strength — persistent operating/cash buffer (Analyst Interpretation).** P reports CFO/sales of 25.755668% in FY2024 and 20.880790% in FY2023, and CFO-minus-gross-cash-capex of 1880 and 1236 USDm. Together with above-cohort operating margins in both years, this supports B's earnings-buffer judgment rather than an isolated favorable year. Reported FY2024 sales growth of 20.577069% adds scale context, not an organic-growth explanation. Acquisition contributions, cost classification and mix prevent attributing the advantage wholly to pricing power. Basis: P T4.2–T4.4/T4.6.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Weakness — debt burden and allocation dominate relative operating strength (Analyst Interpretation; Material risk).** P's bridged debt/CFO contrast means stronger operations coexist with greater claims on generated cash. B's debt-funded distribution evidence and committed dividend uses explain why operating progress need not reduce refinancing dependence. Acquisition and dividend cash uses sit outside the cash-after-capex proxy. The strongest countercase is persistent margins, cash generation and reported cash: these could support repayment **if retained and accessible**. Repeated retention and a falling consistently defined debt/CFO burden would improve the view; renewed debt-funded extraction or deteriorating conversion would weaken it. Basis: B priority findings/ranked weaknesses; P T4.4–T4.7 and countercase.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: P does not normalize economic cash. CW and HEICO benefit from customer funding; Moog suffered advance reversals and includes receivable-sale proceeds in CFO, unlike TDG securitization financing. Moog's FY2024 illustrative CFO sensitivity is 177.344 USDm, not restated GAAP CFO. These mechanisms restrict causal claims about cash efficiency. Finance-lease bridging also matters: TDG/HEICO already include finance leases; CW/Moog require additions outside borrowing captions. No double counting or silent operating-lease inclusion is adopted. Basis: P cash-funding and debt-bridge sections.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Valuation caution — not a new financial-strength score (Analyst Interpretation).** V's two indications are distinct point illustrations, not competing estimates to average. Moog's lower-margin systems/industrial mix makes a revenue transfer potentially too restrictive for durable TDG aftermarket economics; conversely, an EBITDA transfer may exaggerate support if TDG margins or cash conversion erode. This is the strongest countercase to rejecting all relevance: durable differentiated earnings could justify economics unlike Moog's. But matched business mix, earnings definitions and complete capitalization must be established before choosing a valuation anchor. Until then, V adds judgment about model dependence, not creditor protection. Basis: V valuation conclusion/alignment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Acquisition discipline — Wencor context only (Analyst Interpretation; Material execution risk).** W's prospective adjusted proforma earnings include a February acquisition and diligence adjustments. Failure to realize recurring cash earnings could delay repayment; conditional bridge funding could introduce rollover pressure if drawn and not replaced. HEICO's stated deleveraging expectation, complementary offerings and unquantified synergies are the strongest countercase, but remain management expectations, not realized outcomes or TDG support. Verified cash conversion, integration and final funding would change the view. Basis: W transaction evidence and credit interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: These are **source-handoff observations, not new calculations**. Rows for FY2024 are times, carrying borrowing-plus-finance-lease debt at respective fiscal ends divided by annual CFO, from P T4.5/controls. FY2025 rows are USD millions from V valuation controls: principal known-components Moog proxy and two separate provisional TDG transfers. Wencor rows are times from W transaction controls, announced consideration divided by prospective CY2023 denominators. Exact artifact hashes are in Sources; all other numerical observations above are likewise copied, not recomputed.

fields.value: Missing evidence is not adverse behavior. Neither the positive Wencor case nor FY2025 proxy evidence retrospectively fills P's FY2024 valuation gaps. No ratings, covenant-capacity conclusions, security decision, default probability or recovery outcome is supplied.
